items.title: NT Wright’s reading requires "Israel" to change its identity in the middle of Paul’s argument. In Romans 11:25, Israel is partially hardened, distinguished from the Gentiles. In verse 26, "all Israel will be saved." In verses 28–29, they remain enemies concerning the gospel, yet beloved because of the fathers, whose calling is irrevocable. That plainly describes unbelieving Israel—not the Church. "In this way" simply explains how salvation comes; it does not redefine who is saved. Paul anticipates Israel’s "fullness" (v. 12), "acceptance" (v. 15), and being grafted back into their own olive tree (vv. 23–24). This means a corporate turning to Messiah, not automatic salvation for every Jewish individual. Calling that expectation a "modern-day fantasy" dismisses the very hope Paul tells Gentile believers not to arrogantly deny. NT Wright's entire argument is incoherent and literally the precise opposite of what Paul the Apostle is articulating. https://t.co/XWrwYx2Wjs
